blockers.title: wishlistStore.hydrate() never called at app startup
blockers.detail: App.tsx's hydrateStores() Promise.all([...]) calls .hydrate() on all 6 other persisted stores (profile/products/routines/procedures/settings/tracking) but wishlistStore was not added to that list (confirmed by repo-wide grep for '.hydrate()' — only call site is the store's own test file). addEntry/removeEntry do persist correctly via saveJson, but on every app restart the store's entries reset to [] and the persisted data is never loaded back. A WishlistEntry saved in one session is invisible in the next — contradicts Story 3's core premise ('save... so I can revisit it later'). Not caught by any test because every qa-lead/engineer test jest.mocks wishlistStore with static state, so none exercise real hydration wiring.
blockers.fix: Add `useWishlistStore.getState().hydrate()` to App.tsx's hydrateStores() Promise.all array, same as the other 6 stores. One line.
blockers.note: Tech design FE-5 never named App.tsx as a file to modify either — worth adding it to the task's file list, this is partly a design-doc gap, not purely an implementation miss.

blockers.title: ManualProductFormScreen's explorePrefill branch never pre-fills brand/name
blockers.detail: Spec Story 5 AC1 (approved): the shared completion form must open 'pre-filled with whatever the entry already has (brand, name, category, parsed ingredients)' when promoting a WishlistEntry. The explorePrefill branch in the prefill useEffect only calls setFullIngredientText/setSelectedIngredients/setProductType — never setBrand/setName, unlike the ocrPrefill branch immediately above it which does call setBrand/setName when present. A WishlistEntry promoted via 'Move to Shelf' typically already has brand+name (captured during the Story 3 Save-to-Wishlist prompt), so this shows an empty form and forces the user to retype data they already entered.
blockers.fix: Add `if (explorePrefill.brand) setBrand(explorePrefill.brand); if (explorePrefill.name) setName(explorePrefill.name);` alongside the existing category-prefill line.
blockers.note: qa-lead's own EXPLORE_PREFILL test fixture hardcodes brand:null,name:null even in the wishlistEntryId-present test cases, so the existing suite structurally can't catch this — qa-lead should add a non-null-brand/name case once fixed.

comparison_matrix_4_parameters (not 5): functional profile breadth (buildCapabilities() tag count, reused from §3.1), ingredient count (tokenizeRawText().length, reused from §3.3), active tags (resolved.resolvedActiveKeys from resolveFromRawText directly, never getProductActiveKeys()), category-relative signal (the captured category). The originally-proposed 5th parameter (skin-type suitability) was removed from the matrix entirely.

comparison_basis: user's own productsStore items filtered to the same category only, nothing else (no corpus/aggregate data exists in this app); zero same-category items renders a plain message, never a fabricated comparison.

skin_type_caution_signal: standalone element, NOT a matrix parameter. Fires on properties.exfoliating===true OR properties.photosensitizing===true OR properties.irritancy>=3, regardless of any barrierRepair counterpart (the deliberately 'loosened' definition, human-confirmed via a 500-composition coverage check: 15.2% vs 6.8%). Renders nothing at all (~85% case) when it doesn't fire. Names the real triggering active(s) + the user's stored profile.skinType in a genuine sentence when it does fire; null skinType suppresses it even if otherwise triggered (planner assumption).
